name: Amphipolis
text: Amphipolis (Greek: Αμφίπολη, romanized: Amfipoli; Ancient Greek: Ἀμφίπολις, romanized: Amphipolis) was an important ancient Greek polis (city), and later a Roman city, whose large remains can still be seen. It gave its name to the modern municipality of Amphipoli, in the Serres regional unit of Northern Greece. Amphipolis was originally a colony of ancient Athens and was the site of the battle between the Spartans and Athenians in 422 BC.

depictions.name: Amphipolis
depictions.text: Amphipolis (Ancient Greek: Ἀμφίπολις) is a municipality in Makedonia, Greece, that was once a polis in classical anitquity. During the Peloponnesian War, the city played a strategic and economic role due to the nearby silver mines. Originally settled by the Athenians, the city was subsequently captured by Brasidas of Sparta in 424 BCE.
